profile.reading: This building, SFO3, sits at 1400 Kifer Road in Sunnyvale, California, part of Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster. Unlike the SFO1, SFO2, and SFO4 codes elsewhere in this cluster, which each cover two separate buildings, Csquare own SEC registration prospectus lists only a single unit under the SFO3 code, designated SFO3_A, a leased rather than company-owned facility of 19,958 rentable square feet, 82.8 percent occupied as of March 31, 2026, giving this record an unusually clean one-to-one match between the OpenStreetMap building and the company own property table. Csquare, Inc., trading on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR, is the current name of a data center real estate company whose Silicon Valley facilities trace back to CenturyLink Savvis-heritage colocation assets, divested and rebranded Evoque Data Center Solutions around 2020 to 2021 under Brookfield-affiliated ownership, later Centersquare, and now Csquare ahead of its July 16, 2026 initial public offering. That IPO priced at 21 dollars per share across 50 million shares for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross, and Brookfield Corporation retained approximately 69 percent of voting power afterward, making Csquare a controlled company under NYSE rules. Per the same prospectus, the company overall portfolio as of March 31, 2026 spanned 64 sites across 21 major metro markets in the US, Canada, and the UK, totaling roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity and more than 1,700 customers, with CEO Spencer Mullee and CFO Steven Cook both having joined from the company Evoque-era leadership. No tenant is named for SFO3 specifically in any source reviewed. Sunnyvale sits between San Jose and Mountain View in the heart of Silicon Valley, and the Kifer Road corridor near this building has long hosted a mix of enterprise office and light-industrial buildings, several of which have been converted to data center or telecom use over the decades, consistent with this facility CenturyLink Savvis-heritage origins described above and its current leased, rather than owned, status in Csquare portfolio.
profile.research_note: SFO3 is the one code in this cluster with a single OSM building and a single SEC S-1 property entry (SFO3_A, 19,958 rentable sqft, leased, 82.8% occupied), so this figure is confidently assigned to this specific record unlike the paired SFO1/SFO2/SFO4 buildings elsewhere in the cluster. Company background from the same filing.

reading.body:
Csquare SFO3 in Sunnyvale publishes 129.4 MW of combined utility power across 273,000 square feet of technical space. The spec does not break that figure into IT load versus overhead, so the usable compute capacity is not determinable from published data alone. Treating the full 129.4 MW as a rough upper bound on IT load, and assuming 40 kW per rack as a common AI training density, the campus could support on the order of 3,200 racks. At the higher densities now common for GPU clusters, 80 to 100 kW per rack, the same power envelope would shrink rack count to roughly 1,300 to 1,600 racks. Power, not floor space, is the binding variable here.

The six certifications qualify this campus to host workloads with specific compliance requirements. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attest to audited controls over financial reporting and operational security. PCI DSS qualifies the facility for payment card data environments. ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53 qualify it for information security management and federal-aligned security frameworks respectively. LEED indicates a rating for energy and environmental design, though the level is not published on the operator's spec page.

Within California, this site ranks eighth by published megawatts among the facilities tracked here, and California has 103 mapped facilities of which only seven publish a megawatt figure at all. The seven facilities with published figures total 185 MW combined, and SFO3's 129.4 MW represents approximately 70 percent of that published total. This concentration reflects how rarely operators publish capacity figures rather than a claim that this campus dominates the state's actual installed base.
